fields.description: Why the last go-live attempt parked this agent — surfaced as a form intro banner, not a field. Cleared automatically when the agent leaves Needs Attention.
fields.label: Needs Attention Reason

fields.description: LLM temperature (0.0 = deterministic, 2.0 = creative)
fields.label: Temperature

fields.description: Max output tokens. 0 = use global default
fields.label: Max Tokens

fields.description: JSON list of required runtime variables. Format: [{"name": "var_name", "description": "What it contains"}]
fields.label: Required Variables

fields.description: Worked examples and non-negotiable rules. Both are part of the frozen static context layer: examples demonstrate, guard rails constrain, and neither changes between turns of a conversation.
fields.label: Examples & Guard Rails

fields.description: Few-shot examples. Rendered after the system prompt, in row order, into the immutable static context layer.
fields.label: Examples

fields.description: Rules the agent must obey on every turn. Rendered last in the static context layer so they are the final word.
fields.label: Guard Rails

fields.description: For agents with multiple sub-agents (e.g., Report Query Agent)
fields.label: Sub Prompts

fields.description: LangSmith project name for this agent. Leave blank to use the global project from Processa Settings.
fields.label: LangSmith Project

fields.description: The BPMN process map that runs this agent. Tools are granted by the shapes drawn in this diagram — never listed on this document.
fields.label: Process Model

fields.description: Grants this agent the right to create other AI Agent Configurations. Exactly one configuration on the site may hold the grant, and it must link the process below.
fields.label: Can Create Agents

fields.description: The BPMN process map that carries a newly created agent from Draft to Live. Looked up from this field — its name is never assumed.
fields.label: Agent Creation Process

fields.description: The agent's model, picked from the catalog. The provider below follows from this model's credentials link.
fields.label: AI Model

fields.description: Derived from the linked AI Model — the model is the pick, its provider follows. Supplies the API key and the request dialect for every call this agent makes.
fields.label: AI Provider

fields.description: Stamped on Chat Conversation.agent_mode and matched by the map's start condition.
fields.label: Chat Mode Label

fields.description: Opening message the shared chat panel shows for this agent. Markdown allowed. Empty = no greeting bubble.
fields.label: Greeting

fields.description: Input hint in the chat composer, e.g. "Describe the script change…".
fields.label: Composer Placeholder

fields.description: How the agent hands work over: Conversation = it only talks, nothing to apply. Document = offers a new version of something to accept or reject. Form = fills in fields to confirm. (Not the runner — that is Agent Framework.)
fields.label: Surface Type

fields.description: What the thing it produces actually is — selects the preview renderer and the apply target (Script→editor, Diagram→canvas, Schema→builder, Record→form).
fields.label: Artifact Type

fields.description: Show thumbs up / down on this agent's replies. Turn off for agents whose answers are not a judgement call, where a rating would only be noise.
fields.label: Collect Response Feedback

fields.description: Leave empty to allow every logged-in user.
fields.label: Allowed Roles

fields.description: Who this agent acts as when its tools change something, and what it is allowed to change. Always shown, whatever kind of agent this is — a Background agent is the one most likely to need a role, and these fields used to be hidden on exactly those.
fields.label: Identity & Permissions

fields.description: The identity this agent acts as. Created automatically and never logged into by a person: what an agent changed is attributable to the agent, and its write access is granted and revoked here rather than in code. Distinct from Allowed Roles, which says who may INVOKE the agent.
fields.label: Agent User

fields.description: What this agent may do when its tools write. Its user holds exactly these roles — adding one grants a permission, removing one revokes it, with no deployment. Leave empty and the agent can read what everyone can read and change nothing.
fields.label: Roles the Agent Holds

fields.description: Controls applied to this agent's traffic before it reaches a model provider.
fields.label: Security

fields.description: Screens the user's message for Kuwait Civil IDs, contact details, passport and travel document numbers, and bank or payment details, replacing each with a token (e.g. [CIVIL_ID_1]) before the text reaches the model or the conversation log. Tokens are swapped back for the real value when the agent calls a tool, so lookups still work. Disable only for an agent whose work genuinely needs the raw values in the prompt — and record why.
fields.label: PII Input Screening

fields.description: What to do when the agent's OWN response contains a credential, personal data, or a stretch of its own instructions. Flag (the default) records it and replaces the offending text with a token, so the reply still reads. Log records it and sends the reply untouched — use it to watch a new agent before tightening. Block replaces the whole reply with a refusal.
fields.label: Output Screening Mode

fields.description: Screens the user's message against the AI Injection Pattern rule pack before it reaches the model — instruction overrides ("ignore your previous instructions"), jailbreak personas, attempts to extract the system prompt, and tool-abuse phrasing. Disable only for an agent whose ordinary traffic trips the pack constantly, and record why: a disabled screen still lets the turn run, but nothing is watched.
fields.label: Injection Screening

fields.description: What to do when a rule fires on the user's message. Flag (the default) removes the matched phrase and lets the turn continue on the rest — the attack is defused without the user losing their request. Log records it and sends the message through untouched; use it to watch a new agent before tightening. Block refuses the turn and tells the user why. Every outcome is recorded as an AI Security Event either way.
fields.label: Injection Action

fields.description: How hard this agent pushes back: how fast one user may talk to it, and how many blocked attempts it tolerates before freezing the conversation. Both are per-agent — a limit that suits a chat assistant throttles a batch agent to a standstill — and both are governed by the one switch below. Who may RELEASE a freeze stays site-wide, on Processa Settings.
fields.label: Rate Limiting & Freeze

fields.description: The switch for this whole section — both the throttle and the freeze. Off exempts this agent only, not the site, and means no throttling AND no freezing. A conversation already frozen stays frozen until a reviewer releases it.
fields.label: Enable Rate Limiting

fields.description: Messages one user may send this agent inside the window. 0 disables the throttle.
fields.label: Messages Per Window

fields.description: The window slides continuously rather than resetting on a clock boundary, so a full allowance cannot be sent twice either side of one.
fields.label: Window (seconds)

fields.description: Blocked attempts by one user against THIS agent before the conversation is frozen and a reviewer has to release it. Counted per ATTEMPT: one message that trips several rules is one strike. 0 disables the freeze while leaving the throttle on. To keep the freeze WITHOUT a throttle, set Messages Per Window to 0 instead of unticking Enable Rate Limiting.
fields.label: Freeze After N Blocked Attempts

fields.description: Eval suites now link to this agent from the suite side — see the Evaluation group in the Connections panel above to view or add suites. (The former Evaluation Suite field was removed.)
fields.label: Evaluation

fields.description: Baseline evaluation cases are generated from these.
fields.label: Sample Prompts

fields.description: How this agent remembers. These settings are authoritative at dispatch — the BPMN shape no longer stores them; an older diagram's values are still honoured until the agent is configured here.
fields.label: Memory

fields.description: Where this agent's message thread is kept. Process Variable lives in the instance and is discarded with it; Document Store persists. Blank inherits the diagram's value.
fields.label: Conversation Store

fields.description: Most recent messages kept when priming a call; the system prompt is always retained. 0 inherits the diagram's value.
fields.label: Context Window (max messages)

fields.description: Recall relevant saved memories before the call, and optionally save one after. Blank inherits the diagram's value.
fields.label: Long-Term Memory

fields.description: Agent — this task; Process — this process model; Entity — the task's context document.
fields.label: Memory Scope

fields.description: Distilled extracts durable, deduplicated facts; Raw stores the agent output verbatim (legacy); Off recalls only.
fields.label: Memory Write Mode

fields.description: Which model does the memory writes. Falls back to the Processa Settings default, then to this agent's own AI Model — so leaving both blank keeps today's behaviour.
fields.label: Memory Models

fields.description: Model that extracts durable facts from a run. A cheaper/faster model is usually fine here.
fields.label: Distillation Model

fields.description: Model that decides add / update / replace against existing memories. Raise this one when reconciliations are poor.
fields.label: Reconciliation Model

fields.description: Expose this agent to approved A2A clients. The agent card is served publicly only while the agent is enabled and Live.
fields.label: Exposed over A2A

fields.description: Comma-separated tags advertised on the agent card, e.g. backend, frappe, python.
fields.label: A2A Skill Tags

fields.description: Leave off and this agent may hand work to any agent exposed over A2A — normally what you want, since the tools drawn on its process map already decide who it actually calls. Tick it only to narrow that to a named few.
fields.label: Restrict Delegation to Specific Agents

fields.description: The only agents this agent may hand work to while the restriction above is on. Each entry is an INDEPENDENT agent with its own configuration, map and lifecycle — this list grants permission to delegate, it does not create or own a child agent. Add, remove or reorder freely; the change takes effect immediately, with no code push and no restart.
fields.label: Allowed Delegates

fields.description: Maximum parent-to-sub-agent nesting level (A → B → C = 3). Exceeding it stops the chain instead of looping.
fields.label: Max Recursion Depth

fields.description: Maximum total handoffs in one task chain. Catches sideways loops that nesting depth alone misses. A bulk request counts as one delegation.
fields.label: Max Task Handoffs

fields.description: How long this agent may take on work handed to it before the delegating step gives up. A step can override it; blank falls back to 240.
fields.label: Deadline When Delegated To (minutes)

fields.description: Retry attempts for a failed sub-agent call before the delegation is marked failed.
fields.label: Max Delegation Retries

fields.description: How many times this agent may ask the story owner about one piece of work before it stops asking and the question is raised with the process owner instead. 0 means no limit. Worth setting: the measured failure of an agent allowed to ask is over-asking — a question that adds friction without improving the outcome.
fields.label: Max Clarification Rounds
